items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: I took a couple lessons with Armando Ghitalla

ctx.x: Yeah. We would start the feast on the day before and we would start at 8 in the morning. Italian bands, however, don’t march in step, they just walk. They don’t march in step, they just walk and play. Because all the marches, the old Italian marches, they’re like little overtures, They’re not like “Stars and Stripes Forever” all the way through it. They’re very musical and everybody doesn’t play at once and it’s like a little mini- overture. So we used to do that 8 to 12 noon, and take a break and then go across…

numbers while they shot the fireworks. And we did the same thing the next day. And four trumpets. We all did all of it. And I guess nobody ever told us we were supposed to get tired. But we just played. It took a lot of endurance. Along those lines, while I was doing “Funny Girl” we opened in Boston and I took a couple lessons with Armando Ghitalla and the first thing he asked me, I played something and he liked it and he said, “Tell me a little bit about your background.” And I told him I played — my father has…

I find it deliciously ironic that I was listening to another interview with you and you were describing something that we’ll get to eventually today but playing in Las Vegas and your day ran from 2 PM to 4 AM. It almost sounds like the same schedule, like 50 years later.
